procedural_matters: PUR 2884 asked for more time to prepare. The hearing was postponed until 18:10.
PUR 2884 stated at 18:10 that she has had enough time to prepare.
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
GER 3160 was represented by Olha Lubianska.
PUR 2884 was represented by Diego Rivera.
facts: At the time of the incident, the wind speed was 20 knots with choppy sea.
In race F5 of the Silver fleet, about 20 - 25 seconds before the start, GER 3160 was on starboard tack sailing slowly towards the starting line.
PUR 2884 approached from clear astern of GER 3160 on a reach.
PUR 2884 established an overlap to leeward of GER 3160.
Immediately thereafter, the starboard bow of PUR 2884 collided with the port quarter of GER
There was damage to the port quarter of GER 3160, which is a split ranging from the aft quarter approximately 20 cm forward along the sheer line.
conclusions: When acquiring right-of-way through her own actions, PUR 2884 failed to initially give GER 3160 room to keep clear, and broke RRS 15.
PUR 2884 failed to avoid contact with GER 3160 when it was reasonably possible and broke RRS 14(a).
GER 3160 was to windward of PUR 2884 and failed to keep clear of PUR 2884 and broke RRS
Since GER 3160 broke RRS 11 while she was sailing within the room to which she was entitled under RRS 15, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.
It was not reasonable possible for GER 3160 to avoid contact and therefore she did not break RRS 14(a).
decision: PUR 2884 is DSQ in Race F5.
